In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
squab exposure stimulates fos expression in a number of brain areas involved in parental behavior.
the POA, hypothalamus, and lateral septal nuclei are activated by squab exposure and the POA and lateral septal regions are activated by tactile exposure to young.
the POA and LH appear to be involved in the parental behavior of the ring dove.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the POA is activated by squab exposure and the POA, lateral septum, and LH are activated by tactile contact with young.
the POA and LH are important for parenting behavior, and the POA may be involved in both appetitive and consummatory aspects of parenting.
squab exposure stimulates fos-like immunoreactive neurons in the medial pre-optic nucleus, lateral septum, lateral hypothalamus, bed nucleus of stria terminalis and pre-optic area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tactile and nontouch contact with young can stimulate fos-ir in several brain areas that are known or suspected to be involved in parenting.
the POA and LH are involved in the appetitive aspects of parental care, whereas the lateral septum is involved in the consummatory aspects of parental care.
parental responses to their young are not simply a function of contact with them but also depend on the type of contact.
